text:
Maya: heads-up — I’m about to land the quantized kernel changes (quant-kernel v3.2.1) into main. Before merge I want a very small premerge rollout plan + clear fallback guardrails. tagging @Dan @Zhao @Tiffany @Juan and ops.

Dan: :eyes: thanks. quick checklist please: smoke metrics, matmul latency, kv-cache integrity, and rollback trigger thresholds.

Zhao: on telemetry — add a 1m QPS-weighted matmul p95, and a KV cache miss-rate alert. If matmul p95 > +15% for 5m or kv-miss > 2% sustained for 3m, trigger rollback.

Maya: agreed. I’ll also require a tiny traffic slice first (0.5% -> 5% -> 25%) with 10m observation windows between steps.

Tiffany: note for release notes — include compatibility caveat for int8-packed weights and list models we’ve validated. I’ll draft RN and post link before merge.

Juan: Dedicated customers: request we pin the dedicated pool to kernel v3.1.x for 2h fallback window. If any rollback, we flip routing back to v3.1.x for those customers. Ops: can we automate that?

OpsBot: deploy-window available tonight 00:30-02:00 UTC. Canary automation supports staged traffic slices and automatic revert on alert.

Dan: add a deploy-bot preflight that runs the following smoke job and fails fast:
```bash
deploy-bot preflight --job quant-matmul-smoke --env staging --timeout 600
# expects max 2% perf regression and no kv-cache errors
```

BuildBot: CI build 3.2.1-rc passed on linux-gpu, mac sim; quant profile benchmarks show median perf -1.2% vs baseline. Artifacts: gs://redwood-builds/quant-kernel/3.2.1-rc

Zhao: small config suggestion — throttle sample size per region to avoid regional hot-spots. Config I’d use: 
```json
{"stages": [{"pct": 0.5, "duration_min": 10}, {"pct": 5, "duration_min": 10}, {"pct": 25, "duration_min": 20}], "rollback_triggers": {"matmul_p95_pct": 15, "kv_miss_pct": 2}}
```

Maya: perf gating accepted. Also enable KV cache prefix snapshotting for the first 30m to ensure we can validate content parity.

Tiffany: RN draft: https://docs.internal.redwood/release-notes/quant-kernel-3-2-1-draft (will add validated model list).

Juan: ops note: if we need to flip dedicated back, use `routing set-version --pool dedicated-prod --version v3.1.x --reason "quant rollback"` — do we want a short runbook in the thread?

Dan: yes please. Add quick steps and assign an owner for the first 2h after deploy. I can be on-call for handoffs.

Maya: assigning owners: Dan (first responder), Zhao (telemetry triage), Juan (dedicated routing), Tiffany (RN/comms). I’ll tag in post-deploy smoke.

OpsBot: enqueue job: `deploy-bot rollout --artifact gs://redwood-builds/quant-kernel/3.2.1-rc --stages 0.5,5,25 --watch-alerts` scheduled for 00:45 UTC. Reply `+1` to confirm.

Maya: +1. I’ll hold merge until RN link and the preflight pass are in the thread.

BuildBot: preflight result: PASS (matmul p95 delta +0.8%, kv-miss 0.1%). Artifacts promoted to candidate.

Zhao: telemetry hooks created: dashboards + alerting. I added a short-lived perf histogram and KV integrity check.

Tiffany: RN updated and published to the internal doc. Adding the canary schedule and rollback playbook section.

Juan: pinned dedicated pool shelved for 2h; automation ready to toggle.

Maya: merging in 5. Will monitor first slice. If anything flaps, we revert and enact the dedicated pin routing.

Dan: standing by. If we see noisy signals, call a quick rollback with reason and screenshot the graphs.

OpsBot: rollout started: stage 1 (0.5%) -> observing.

Maya: stage 1 metrics look stable after 10m. moving to 5%.

BuildBot: stage 2 deployed -> observing 10m. matmul p95 +1.1%, KV-miss 0.3%. all green.

Zhao: watch for slow climb in p95; I’ll alert if it crosses +12% sustained 5m.

Maya: moving to 25% per plan.

OpsBot: stage 3 (25%) done. No auto-triggered rollback.

Tiffany: RN live and slack announcement queued on release channel.

Juan: dedicated pool pin left in place for 1.5h in case of delayed regressions.

Dan: thanks team. If we get flakiness post 30m, apply routing flip and open an incident. Otherwise I’ll close the thread after 2h clear.

Maya: closing loop — initial rollout complete, no rollback. Will file post-deploy note and follow up on any model-specific regressions. :tada:
